profile.headline: Software Developer at Epic | Web dev, game dev, and recreational programming
profile.summary:
Hi! I’m Aubrey, a software engineer specializing in game development, software engineering, and full-stack web development, with over 6 years of indie game experience and 8 years of indie web development.

In game development, I’ve built numerous projects across Unity and Godot, using C#, C++, and GDScript. I’m deeply familiar with all core engine systems, including rendering pipelines, physics, AI, UI, sound, and tooling, and I thrive on tackling complex technical challenges. My interests also includes engine development, where I’ve explored render pipelines, physics simulation, operating systems, and scheduling algorithms.

On the web side, I bring 8 years of experience designing and implementing responsive and accessible interfaces. I worked at the Center of World Languages for two years, developing three major websites using an ASP.NET backend. My personal projects often leverage React, Next.js, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript and CSS features. I’m experienced with both serverless architectures and microservices, integrating databases, caching, and third-party APIs seamlessly.

I’m also passionate about programming languages. I’ve written code in nearly all major languages, including C, C++, Rust, C#, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Python, and I’m interested in language design and compiler development. I love open-source software and actively contribute to and create reusable libraries, primarily in C++ using CMake.

I take pride in bridging the gap between creative design and robust engineering, whether building immersive games, performant systems, or elegant web applications.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.locationName: Los Angeles, California, United States · Hybrid
positions.description: In charge of managing, designing, and implementing full-stack websites using ASP.NET WebForms in Visual Basic with an in-house CMS, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with jQuery for the frontend. Designed end-to-end the websites for UCLA's Center for World Languages, the National Heritage Language Resource Center, and the Coalition for Community-Based Heritage Languages Schools using accessible and responsive designs.
positions.insights: Skills: Full-Stack Development · Figma (Software) · JavaScript · ASP.NET Web Forms · Google Material Design

positions.title: Lead Web Developer and Workshop Chair
positions.locationName: Los Angeles, California, United States · On-site
positions.description:
During this role, I served as the lead web developer and co-chair of workshops.

As the lead web developer, I pitched the idea for a website to the organization, and after organized a team of members to design and implement the website. I helped with Design alongside other members, where we crafted mockups in Figma. I then led development, which used Next.js and React with MUI, which we completed in 2024. 

As an officer, I created numerous workshops teaching many game development topics, including artificial intelligence, user interfaces, graphics and shaders, Git, and editor tooling. As a workshop co-chair, I helped plan, schedule, assign, and assist with workshops made by members during the schoolyear. I also pitched and helped create a new workshop track called Roguelike Series, where we constructed 8 workshops tailored to get students to create a roguelike game end-to-end in a quarter.
positions.insights: Skills: Game Development · Full-Stack Development · Teaching

positions.title: Academic Student Instructor
positions.locationName: Los Angeles, California, United States · On-site
positions.description: Constructed interactive lesson plans, homework, and projects for a 10-week UCLA seminar teaching fundamental systems of the Unity game engine. Taught course in Fall 2024, where students in groups produced 3 game-jam sized games.

company.name: UCLA Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Developer for a simple web application for giving users who have donated money to the Coronado Schools Foundation a Locals Card. It also uses the Google Maps API to show supported businesses that allow usage of the Locals Card.
Left development due to school.

projects.title: Death Party
projects.description: Game developed by Sunday Studios Games. 3D narrative-driven puzzle game where you investigate the death of your friend at a frat party. I am responsible for implementing assets, working on systems like inventory management, UI, and saving.

projects.title: Tune Collector
projects.description: Tune Collector is a submission to Ludum Dare 58 for the theme Collector. We decided to make a rhythm game with deckbuilder mechanics, where you would build out "tunes" to deal damage to enemies, but you would have to play the tunes in a rhythm game style for them to work.
